findings.trigger: Model training vs real-time inference on identical transaction records with categorical features (merchant_category, country_code, device_type).
findings.expected_behavior: Training and inference must map categorical values to identical numeric representations and scale all features with identical reference bounds (Gate E).
findings.actual_behavior: DataGenerator.encode_features used pandas alphabetical .astype('category').cat.codes and batch-dynamic min-max scaling, whereas predict.py used fixed list indices (MERCHANT_CATEGORIES.index) and REFERENCE_BOUNDS. For example, 'grocery' was code 11 at training (alphabetical) but index 0 at inference, corrupting model inputs at test time.
findings.root_cause: Ad-hoc pandas categorical encoding in synthetic data generator was not synchronized with serving router reference bounds and authoritative category lists.
findings.prediction_metric_impact: Model was trained on one feature representation and evaluated on a severely corrupted representation, artificially reducing inference predictive capability.
findings.proof: Comparing DataGenerator.encode_features(pd.DataFrame([sample])) with preprocess_transaction(sample) yielded large numerical differences across categorical columns.
findings.repair_strategy: Standardized DataGenerator.encode_features to use authoritative MERCHANT_CATEGORIES, COUNTRIES, and DEVICES list indices and shared REFERENCE_BOUNDS, enforcing exact FEATURE_NAMES schema ordering.

findings.trigger: First 5 warmup transactions evaluated in model governance store all contain negative (legitimate) labels (actual_label == 0).
findings.expected_behavior: When ground truth data contains only one class, ROC-AUC is mathematically undefined. Governance auto-rollback should only trigger on genuine performance degradation, not on single-class warmup data.
findings.actual_behavior: safe_roc_auc_score returned fallback default=0.5. ModelEvaluationEngine evaluated `champ_auc < 0.65` (0.5 < 0.65 -> True) and triggered a spurious auto-rollback of the champion model.
findings.root_cause: Fallback sentinel 0.5 was treated as a genuine measured performance drop below 0.65 rather than distinguishing mathematically undefined status.
findings.prediction_metric_impact: Valid promoted champion models were spuriously rolled back during initial production traffic windows whenever fraud cases were temporarily absent.
findings.proof: Logging 5 legitimate feedback records (actual_label=0) caused rollback_triggered=True and reverted champion to v1.
findings.repair_strategy: Added `has_both_classes = len(set(y_true)) >= 2` guard before evaluating `champ_auc < 0.65` in ModelEvaluationEngine.evaluate_performance. Enhanced safe_roc_auc_score with is_roc_auc_defined and compute_roc_auc_with_status.

findings.trigger: Executing batch prediction on a list containing transaction A compared to single prediction on transaction A when feature_store_enabled is True.
findings.expected_behavior: Single-record inference and equivalent one-record batch inference must agree within numerical tolerance (MODEL-INV-10).
findings.actual_behavior: predict_transaction queried online feature store to enrich transaction features (velocity, customer_history_score, etc.), while predict_batch skipped feature store enrichment entirely and evaluated raw payload dictionaries, causing predictions to diverge.
findings.root_cause: Online feature store retrieval was only implemented in the single-record route and omitted from the batch route.
findings.prediction_metric_impact: Batch scoring produced different risk decisions than real-time single transaction scoring for the exact same transaction payload.
findings.proof: Inspected code in predict_batch showing raw payload passed directly to preprocess_transaction without feature store enrichment.
findings.repair_strategy: Added online feature store batch query and enrichment in predict_batch before tensor preprocessing, guaranteeing identical feature inputs.

findings.trigger: Submitting transaction features containing non-finite floats (NaN, +Inf, -Inf).
findings.expected_behavior: Inference boundary must fail closed and reject non-finite inputs before forward pass execution (MODEL-INV-13).
findings.actual_behavior: preprocess_transaction clipped values using max(0.0, min(1.0, val)) where Python min/max on NaN can produce corrupt zeroes or NaNs, and _eval_model did not validate finite output.
findings.root_cause: Missing explicit math.isfinite checks on raw input values and model outputs.
findings.prediction_metric_impact: Risk of silent propagation of NaN tensors through PyTorch layers producing invalid probabilities or unhandled server crashes.
findings.proof: Passed float('nan') into preprocess_transaction which did not raise ValueError.
findings.repair_strategy: Added explicit math.isfinite validation on all numeric features in preprocess_transaction and on model output in _eval_model and _eval_model_batch.

findings.trigger: Loading a simulation model trained with dp_compatible=False (BatchNorm1d) or corrupt state dict.
findings.expected_behavior: Model loader must dynamically detect norm layer architecture (GroupNorm vs BatchNorm1d) and fail closed on corrupt state dicts (MODEL-INV-04 & MODEL-INV-13).
findings.actual_behavior: _get_cached_serving_model hardcoded `dp_compatible=True` when instantiating simulation models and silently caught load_state_dict exceptions, continuing with random uninitialized weights.
findings.root_cause: Hardcoded dp_compatible parameter and overly broad try/except block falling back to random model instantiation.
findings.prediction_metric_impact: Severe: customer transactions could be scored by an untrained randomly-initialized neural network while the system reported successful inference.
findings.proof: Inspected predict.py lines 148-152 where load failure caught Exception and logged warning while returning random weights.
findings.repair_strategy: Updated _get_cached_serving_model to dynamically inspect running_mean/running_var for dp_compatible detection, detect input_dim from weights, and raise HTTP 500 on load failure.
